title: synchronized versus volatile
context: What is the difference between synchronized and volatile?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java concurrency questions (2 of 3)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: `volatile` makes single reads and writes of one variable visible across threads. It does not lock, so a compound update is still a race. `synchronized` makes a block of code mutually exclusive and also guarantees visibility of everything inside it. It blocks other threads and costs more. Use volatile for a flag or a value written by one thread and read by many. Use synchronized, or a lock, when several variables must change together.

points.title: Atomicity
points.why: synchronized makes a block atomic. volatile does not.

points.title: Cost
points.why: volatile reads are cheap. synchronized blocks other threads while it is held.
